due_when.clears_when: exit_lever_ablation.py --grade holdout writes the declared arm's held-back n/net_r beside the selected arm's and labels a selected arm that trails it, OR the operator decides config-change proposals do not need the incumbent comparison

what: [research][promotion-bar] The R-HOLDOUT bar can CONFIRM a challenger that is WORSE than the configuration already trading. exit_lever_ablation.py --grade holdout selects one arm from 9 on discovery and reads ONLY that arm on the held-back span; PASS = 'selected arm net R > 0 there'. It never reads the declared arm A on the same span. MEASURED 2026-10-18 by scripts/research/holdout_incumbent_compare.py over the 8 committed RQ-20261016-077e-* runs (population: each run's own boundary; held-back = trades entered on/after it; full cost stack; every selected-arm figure reproduces verdict.holdout exactly): of 6 runs that read a holdout, 3 PASS verdicts selected an arm the declared arm BEATS on the same span -- xrp_pullback_2h C5 +4.87R n=90 vs A +17.36R n=93 (-12.49R); trend_donchian_xrp_4h C1 +4.13R n=25 vs A +5.48R n=25 (-1.35R); trend_donchian_sol_prop C5 +5.28R n=96 vs A +6.56R n=100 (-1.29R). The other 3 selected arms lead A by +1.00..+2.66R (ada C7, eth_4h C3, slv C1) and iaum C4 is underpowered. Consequence: a mandate or a session reading 'PASS/confirmed' as 'ship the selected arm' would replace a better incumbent (lane HOLDOUT-PROPOSALS-1018 declined to open those 3 Tier-3 PRs for exactly this reason). FIX (Tier-1 research tooling, then a Tier-3 bar note): have --grade holdout also report A's held-back n/net_r (A is fixed before the run, so reading it is not a second selection) and label a PASS whose selected arm trails A as 'confirmed_not_better'; MD-PROMOTE-* R-HOLDOUT is unaffected for promotion of the declared config (A selected), only config-CHANGE proposals need it.
